q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings announcement is scheduled for August 26, 2026. Today is August 16, 2026. **Resolution occurs in 10 days.**

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA will provide forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 revenue. Based on the research:

- **NVIDIA's own prior guidance (May 20, 2026)** for Q2 was $91.0B ±2% ($89.2B–$92.8B range)
- **UBS's estimate** for Q3 guidance: $107–$108B
- The research explicitly states UBS "expects NVIDIA to guide for Q3 FY2027 revenue... in the range of $107-108 billion"

The question asks about "forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release" — this means guidance for subsequent quarters announced during the Q2 earnings call.

UBS's $107–$108B Q3 estimate represents a ~17–19% sequential increase from Q2's $91B baseline, which is consistent with NVIDIA's historical growth trajectory during strong demand periods (Blackwell ramp, Rubin platform emerging).

The most likely outcome centers on the **UBS midpoint of approximately $107.5B**, with reasonable variance around this figure reflecting:
- Potential for upside if Blackwell demand and Rubin ramp exceed expectations
- Downside risk from macro headwinds, China restrictions, or competitive pressure
- Standard management conservatism in guidance

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Macro deterioration**: Weaker-than-expected enterprise IT spending or data center capex cycles
- **China headwinds**: Additional restrictions on data center revenue from China (already excluded from current guidance, but could tighten margins on other regions)
- **Competitive pressure**: AMD or Intel gaining material market share in AI accelerators
- **Rubin ramp delays**: If next-generation platform adoption is slower than UBS's 500k GPU/month projection
- **Conservative guidance**: Management culture favoring lower guidance targets for easier beats
- **Inventory corrections**: If customers reduce purchasing following strong Blackwell orders

Downside risk might push guidance toward **$100–$103B**.

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Accelerating Blackwell demand**: Better-than-expected orders from cloud and enterprise customers
- **Rubin early adoption**: If the next-generation platform ramps faster than anticipated
- **China exception**: If U.S. policy allows selective China data center revenue not currently modeled
- **Customer allocation clearing**: Strong demand sustaining through Q3 despite prior quarter strength
- **Market share gains**: Consolidation of NVIDIA's dominant position with limited competition
- **Capacity expansion**: If NVIDIA signals ability to meet demand beyond current projections

Upside risk might push guidance toward **$110–$115B or higher**.

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

**No reliable base rate available** beyond what appears in the research provided. However, the research does provide:
- Specific prior guidance: Q2 FY2027 was projected at $91.0B ±2% (issued May 20, 2026)
- Specific analyst forecast: UBS models $107–$108B for Q3 FY2027 guidance
- Sequential growth context: ~17–19% increase represents strong but not unprecedented for NVIDIA during major platform transitions

The midpoint of UBS's range ($107.5B) serves as the most grounded forecast, with uncertainty distributed symmetrically around it given the 10-day window provides minimal new information.

---

**Reasoning Summary:**
The research provides a specific, credible analyst forecast from a major investment bank (UBS) anchored to the Q3 FY2027 guidance. With only 10 days to resolution and no conflicting recent data, this forecast is the most reliable input available. The range of $107–$108B represents informed consensus expectation. I'll center my estimate on the midpoint with tails reflecting realistic upside (strong Blackwell/Rubin demand) and downside (macro weakness, competitive pressure) risks.

Low (10th percentile): 103000000000
Median (50th percentile): 107500000000
High (90th percentile): 112000000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is scheduled to announce its Q2 FY2027 financial results and host a conference call on August 26, 2026, at 2 p.m. PT (5 p.m. ET) [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-sets-conference-call-for-second-quarter-financial-results-6927195). The Q2 fiscal period concluded on July 26, 2026 [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-sets-conference-call-for-second-quarter-financial-results-6927195).

For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA's own guidance, issued on May 20, 2026, projects revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. This outlook explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

UBS, however, anticipates NVIDIA will surpass its own Q2 guidance, modeling revenue between $94-95 billion for the quarter. More significantly, UBS expects NVIDIA to guide for Q3 FY2027 revenue (October quarter) in the range of $107-108 billion. This higher forecast is attributed to continued strong demand for Blackwell GPUs and an unexpectedly rapid ramp-up of the next-generation Rubin platform, which UBS predicts will reach 500,000 GPU shipments per month [aliteq.com](https://aliteq.com/nvidia-q2-fy27-earnings-preview-ubs-2026).
